claim: For the discrete HCV map (1.6) of Khan–Yaqoob–Alsaadi, assume \(0<g<1\), \(0<\zeta<1\), and \(h>0\). Then the liver-free fixed point \(L=(0,0)\) is a hyperbolic source, because its multipliers are \(\lambda_1=1+h(1-g)>1\) and \(\lambda_2=1+h(1-\zeta)>1\). Consequently, the source's printed sink condition \(h>\max\{2/(g-1),2/(\zeta-1)\}\) is reversed on this biologically relevant parameter domain: both displayed thresholds are negative, so that printed sink inequality holds for every positive \(h\), even though both multipliers have modulus greater than one. For example, \(g=1/2\), \(\zeta=1/3\), and \(h=1\) give \(\lambda_1=3/2\) and \(\lambda_2=5/3\), while the printed thresholds are \(-4\) and \(-3\).
integrity: The Jacobian, multiplier formulas, and printed source/sink inequalities were checked directly against the published full text. The exact witness uses rational arithmetic; no independent audit or external certification is claimed.
scientific_limitations: The result concerns only local stability of the liver-free fixed point on the parameter domain \(0<g<1\), \(0<\zeta<1\), and \(h>0\). It does not establish global dynamics, does not classify all parameter sign regimes, and does not assess the source's partial-infection bifurcation calculations. One later related HCV article was inspected only through its accessible abstract and exposed preview material.
title: The liver-free fixed point is a source throughout the positive boundary-equilibrium regime
